messages:
OncallBot: PAGER — High error rate in eu-west after canary rollout. Alerts: 502/503 spike, elevated latency. Paging on-call: @Maya. Incident ID: INC-2026-176600.
Maya: on it. seeing spike in dashboards, 502s started ~10m after the canary flip. linking logs.
Ethan: grabbing tails. any customer pages yet?
Maya: a few customer errors from EU region, severity P2 so far. 27% request failure for some customers on eu-west-1.
Liam: I can take network/dns checks. Zoe, can you look at routing weights?
Zoe: looking... the blue/green service weights show 90% -> stable(blue), 10% -> canary(green). but DNS A records for eu-west are returning an old IP that matches a decommissioned green node pool in one POP. TTL was 1h but looks like propagation lingered.
Alex: oh no — so clients still hitting green backend even after we changed pool names. that would explain the mismatch.
Maya: logs show upstream failures: 
```
upstream error: server "green-backend-3" returned 503, connection reset
trace_id=xyz123
```
Ethan: can we toggle the region routing feature flag to route 100% to blue while we investigate? Which flag key is it?
Liam: flag is `region-routing-eu` in LaunchDarkly. I can flip to 100% stable.
Zoe: before flipping, we should confirm no in-flight jobs on green that would corrupt state. any stateful writes?
Maya: for this service writes are idempotent; small risk. customer-facing latency is worse if we wait. recommend kill-switch. :thumbsup:
Liam: flipping flag now -> `LD: region-routing-eu = 100% -> blue`
DeployBot: Rollout action recorded. Flag change applied by Liam at 2026-08-19T15:22:07Z. Targeting: eu-west region.
Maya: monitoring... error rate dropping. still seeing tails from some clients with old DNS.
Ethan: can we add a routing rule to the edge to reject requests that hit known-decommissioned-green IPs? I can push a quick deny rule to the eu CDN edge.
Alex: also let's lower the DNS TTL to 30s to accelerate recovery, and open a ticket to fix origin A records for eu-west.
Liam: executed CDN deny rule: `edgectl rule add --region eu-west --drop-ip 10.12.34.56` -> applied.
DeployBot: CDN rule applied by Ethan at 2026-08-19T15:24:55Z.
Maya: big improvement, error rate down to 2.3% now. latency stabilized.
Zoe: confirming backend health, green instances returning 200 for internal probes but with degraded CPU. we'll de-register remaining green nodes from the EU LB.
Liam: de-registered green pool from lb: `gcloud compute backend-services remove-backend ...` -> removed.
PagerDuty: Note: on-call handoff scheduled in 45m. Next on-call: Alex.
Alex: acknowledged, I'll join for the handoff and take post-mortem lead.
Maya: quick customer impact summary for ops report: affected window ~15m, peak failed request rate ~27% for a subset of EU customers, estimated ~1200 failed requests, no data loss. Mitigation: feature-flag kill-switch, CDN deny rule, de-register green backends, updated DNS TTL.
Ethan: creating incident doc link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1766004321-brief (will add timeline + commands).
Zoe: follow-up action items: 1) Audit DNS automation that left stale A records. 2) Add automated test for pool name drift during blue/green. 3) Shorten default DNS TTL during rollouts.
Liam: also add a canary probe that validates backend IPset matches current pool list before flipping weights.
Maya: agreed. I'm going to run a quick retrospective with the oncall rotation. Alex will pick up for final write-up.
Alex: taking over. I'll schedule the postmortem and include annotated timeline + runbook updates. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
OncallBot: Incident INC-2026-176600 marked as mitigated at 2026-08-19T15:37:03Z. Root cause: stale DNS / IP leak to decommissioned green pool during blue/green canary flip.
Maya: closing thread, will post follow-up notes in the incident doc.
Alex: handoff complete. I'll update participants once PM review is in.
DeployBot: Automated rollback not required — configuration changes used rather than full rollback.
Maya: final status: customer-impact P2, services healthy, follow-ups assigned.
